### Numerical Solution
* **Given:** Line voltage $V_L = 400\text{ V}$, $f = 50\text{ Hz}$, Wattmeter readings $W_1 = 300\text{ W}$, $W_2 = 200\text{ W}$.

1. **Active Power ($P$):**
Total active power is the algebraic sum of the two wattmeter readings:
$$P = W_1 + W_2 = 300 + 200 = 500\text{ W}$$ 

2. **Reactive Power ($Q$):**
$$Q = \sqrt{3} (W_1 - W_2) = \sqrt{3} (300 - 200) = 1.732 \times 100 = 173.2\text{ VAR}$$ 

3. **Power Factor Angle ($\phi$) and Power Factor ($\cos\phi$):**
$$\tan\phi = \sqrt{3} \left(\frac{W_1 - W_2}{W_1 + W_2}\right) = \sqrt{3} \left(\frac{300 - 200}{300 + 200}\right) = \sqrt{3} \times \frac{100}{500} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{5} = 0.3464$$
$$\phi = \tan^{-1}(0.3464) = 19.1\degree$$
$$\cos\phi = \cos(19.1\degree) = 0.945 \text{ (lagging)}$$

4. **Line Current ($I_L$):**
$$P = \sqrt{3} V_L I_L \cos\phi$$
$$500 = \sqrt{3} \times 400 \times I_L \times 0.945$$
$$I_L = \frac{500}{654.7} = 0.764\text{ A}$$

* **Results:** Line Current = $0.764\text{ A}$, Active Power = $500\text{ W}$, Reactive Power = $173.2\text{ VAR}$.
proTip: For an inductive load with two wattmeters, $W_1$ is always greater than $W_2$. Total power is $W_1 + W_2$ and reactive power is $\sqrt{3}(W_1 - W_2)$.
